mainTopic: How a Canaanite slave goes free with money or a שטר: through others or by himself, according to רבי מאיר, the חכמים, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
overview: This amud opens by finishing the story of מר זוטרא, who acquired the slave of a dying convert just before the convert died. A second version says the slave was a minor, which fits the תנא קמא of a ברייתא but not אבא שאול, who says minor slaves of a dead convert do not go free. The גמרא then studies the משנה's dispute about how a slave goes free with money or with a שטר. For רבי מאיר, money works only when others pay and a שטר only when the slave receives it himself. The גמרא first explains this as a case where the slave agrees, showing that a slave owns nothing apart from his master, but the שטר clause makes trouble for that answer. אביי and רבא each give a different explanation of why money can work through others while a שטר cannot. Next the גמרא works through the חכמים' words and finally reads them as: money works both ways, but a שטר only through others. That שטר rule belongs to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so there are three opinions. רבה explains his reason by comparing a slave's שטר to a woman's גט. The amud ends as רבה begins a new question.

steps.title: The story ends: one died, one gained
steps.stepSummary: The story of רבי יהודה הינדואה and מר זוטרא closes. The convert died, and מר זוטרא came away with the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (רבי יהודה הינדואה) left this world, and that one (מר זוטרא) left with a living gain, the slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the story it began just before this. The dying convert passed away, and מר זוטרא walked away having acquired the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert with no Jewish heirs leaves ownerless property when he dies. His slaves would then go free on their own. By acquiring the slave while the convert was still alive, מר זוטרא kept him as a slave instead of letting him become free.

phrases.notes: This finishes the story from just before: רבי יהודה הינדואה was dying, and מר זוטרא acquired his slave in time.

phrases.english: and that one departed to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְמִיתָה, וְזֶה פֵּירַשׁ לְחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מר זוטרא acquired the slave right before the convert died, so the slave did not go free.

steps.title: Another version: the slave was a minor
steps.stepSummary: A second version says the slave was a child. That would mean the story does not follow אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the slave was a minor, and this story does not follow אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the story, where the slave was a child. It sets up a ברייתא, coming next, to explain why that matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slave was a minor, מר זוטרא's rush only makes sense if a minor slave would also go free when the convert died. אבא שאול holds that minors do not go free, so by his view מר זוטרא could simply have waited. That is why this version must disagree with אבא שאול.

phrases.english: And there are those who say

phrases.notes: 'He' is the slave that מר זוטרא acquired.

phrases.english: and not in accordance with Abba Shaul,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version the slave was a minor, so the story follows the opinion that minor slaves also go free, not אבא שאול.

steps.title: The ברייתא: do minor slaves of a dead convert go free?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a dead convert's slaves all go free, adults and minors. אבא שאול says only adults go free, and anyone may take the minors.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A convert died and Jews took his property, and it included slaves, both adults and minors. They all become free. אבא שאול says: adults become free, but minors belong to whoever grabs them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that explains the phrase 'not like אבא שאול'. It shows the two opinions about minor slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert with no heirs leaves ownerless property, so his slaves can take themselves free. The תנא קמא says this works even for a child slave. אבא שאול says a child cannot acquire himself, so he stays ownerless property that anyone can take. The second version of the story fits only the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: a convert who died (with no Jewish heirs)

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions agree that adult slaves go free. They argue only about minors.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:

phrases.notes: With no heirs, his property is ownerless, so anyone may take it.

phrases.english: they acquired themselves as free men.
Adults – acquired themselves as free men;
whoever takes possession of them acquires them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind 'not like אבא שאול'.
steps.raayaObject: That the second version of the story disagrees with אבא שאול
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a dispute about minor slaves of a convert who died
steps.whatToRemember: Second version: the slave was a minor, and מר זוטרא had to hurry only because the תנא קמא says even minor slaves go free. אבא שאול disagrees.

steps.title: The משנה: money for freedom must come from others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a slave goes free with money. רבי מאיר says the money must be given by others. The גמרא infers: by others yes, by himself no.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he acquires himself with money, etc.': money given by others. By others, yes, but not by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. The גמרא quotes the משנה about freeing a slave with money and draws a point from רבי מאיר's wording: only others can pay, not the slave himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'by others' suggest the slave himself cannot pay his master to go free. This setup leads into the question that follows: why would that be?

phrases.english: And he acquires himself with money, etc.

phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's opinion in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אִין, אֲבָל לֹא עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the story to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, money given by others frees a slave, but money the slave gives himself does not.

steps.title: What case is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what situation רבי מאיר is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case. It is setting up two possibilities: without the slave's consent, or with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Defining the case will show why the slave himself cannot pay. The answer depends on whether the slave agreed to be freed.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the inference just made.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the slave being freed with or without his consent?

steps.title: It can't be without his consent
steps.stepSummary: If others free him without his consent, that clashes with רבי מאיר's own view that freedom is bad for a slave. You cannot act against someone's interest when he is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means without his consent: we know רבי מאיר says it is a disadvantage for a slave to leave his master for freedom. And we learned: you can benefit someone when he is not there, but you can harm him only when he is there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possibility, that the slave is freed without agreeing, and rejects it. That would contradict רבי מאיר's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that going free is a loss for a slave, since he gives up certain benefits. Acting against someone's interest requires his presence and agreement. So others could not free him without his consent.

keyTerms.meaning: one may benefit a person when he is not present
one may harm him only in his presence

phrases.english: If we say without his consent,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי שְׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר:
phrases.english: after all, we have heard that Rabbi Meir says:
It is a disadvantage for a slave
to leave his master's hand for freedom.
One may act for a person's benefit in his absence,
but one may act against his interest only in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי מאיר means freeing the slave without his consent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds freedom is a loss for the slave, and you may cause someone a loss only in his presence, so others cannot free him without his agreement.

steps.title: So it must be with his consent
steps.stepSummary: The case must be one where the slave agrees. Even then, the משנה teaches that others can pay for him, but he cannot pay himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously with his consent, and this is the lesson: by others, yes; by himself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out 'without consent', the גמרא concludes that the slave agrees. The new point is that even with his agreement, he still cannot pay with his own money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once consent is in place, 'by himself, no' cannot be about consent. It must be about who can hand over the money. That points to a rule about a slave's ownership, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what it teaches us

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously with his consent,
and this is what it teaches us:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining answer after the first was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is with the slave's consent, and still only others can pay the money.

steps.title: A slave owns nothing apart from his master
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion: a slave cannot acquire anything on his own, so he has no money of his own to buy his freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see: a slave has no acquisition without his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the general rule behind רבי מאיר's view. Whatever a slave acquires belongs to his master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any money in the slave's hand already belongs to his master. Paying the master with it would be like paying him with his own money. That is why only others can give money to free him.

keyTerms.meaning: a slave cannot acquire anything apart from his master

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, a slave can go free with money only if others pay. Anything the slave acquires automatically belongs to his master.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that a slave cannot acquire without his master, is a key principle for any discussion of a slave acquiring money, property, or himself.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אֵין קִנְיָן לְעֶבֶד בְּלֹא רַבּוֹ.
phrases.english: Evidently, a slave has no acquisition without his master.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא אֵין קִנְיָן לְעֶבֶד בְּלֹא רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general principle behind the answer just given.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A slave cannot acquire anything independently of his master, so according to רבי מאיר his freedom money must come from others.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה does not fit the 'with his consent' answer
steps.stepSummary: If the case is one where the slave agrees, why does the סיפא say others cannot receive his שטר for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: a slave goes free with a document that he receives himself. Himself, yes; through others, no. But if the slave agrees, why shouldn't others be able to receive it for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 7 (that the case is with the slave's agreement) by using the second half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says a שטר of freedom works only when the slave receives it himself, not through others. If the slave agrees, others should be able to act for him like messengers. So the 'with his consent' answer seems to clash with the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you just said is true
The latter part (end clause) of a משנה
A document; here, the document that frees a slave
By himself; he receives it personally
Through others who receive it for him

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
And if it is with his consent,
why should it not work through others?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7 by pointing to the סיפא of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי מאיר's case is one where the slave agrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the slave agrees, others could receive the שטר for him, yet the סיפא says they cannot.

steps.title: A suggested reading: 'by himself' means 'even by himself'
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the סיפא means the slave can also receive the שטר himself, teaching that his freedom and his power to receive it come at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: what does 'by himself' mean? It means 'even by himself.' The משנה is teaching us that his גט and his 'hand' (his power to receive) come together at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to save the 'with consent' answer: the סיפא is not excluding others, it is adding that even the slave himself can receive it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave normally cannot acquire anything, so one might think he cannot receive his own שטר. The suggestion is that the משנה teaches a new point: at the very moment he gets the שטר, he gains the power to receive it. If so, others really could receive it too.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer the גמרא will test)
His document of freedom and his power to receive come at the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggested answer. The very next step pushes it away, so do not treat it as the conclusion.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ – אַף עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: What does 'by himself' mean? Even by himself,
and this is what it teaches us:
that his document and his hand come as one,
phrases.notes: His 'hand' means his legal power to receive things. He gets it at the same moment he gets the document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'By himself' would mean 'even by himself,' so others are not excluded.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר really excludes others
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying clearly: by himself, and not through others. So the suggested reading fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי מאיר did not teach it that way. A ברייתא says: with a document, by himself and not through others. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested reading by quoting a ברייתא where רבי מאיר clearly says 'not through others.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out 'and not through others,' so 'by himself' cannot mean 'even by himself.' The challenge of step 9 comes back in full: if the slave agrees, why can't others receive it? The 'with consent' answer is now in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: But he did not teach it this way

phrases.english: But he did not teach it this way,
as it was taught: with a document, by himself,
these are the words of רבי מאיר!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reading of step 10 using a ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'even by himself' reading completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא says 'and not through others,' so others are clearly excluded.

steps.title: אביי: the money case works even without the slave's agreement
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case is without the slave's consent. Money is different: since it can transfer him to a new master against his will, it can also transfer him to himself against his will.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the case is without his consent. Money is different. Since money can acquire him against his will, it can also give him to himself against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer. He goes back to the idea that others pay without the slave's agreement, and explains why that is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said you cannot do something bad for a person without his agreement. אביי answers that money is a special case: a slave can be sold with money from one master to another without asking him. So money can also free him without asking him, even though freedom is bad for him in רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually (returns to an earlier idea)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the רישא and סיפא of the משנה together. With money others can act even without his agreement, but with a שטר only the slave himself can receive it.

phrases.english: אביי said: Really, it is without his consent,
since it acquires him against his will,
phrases.notes: When one master sells the slave to another with money, the slave's agreement is not needed.

phrases.english: it transfers him to himself against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the 'with consent' answer, which failed in steps 9 to 11, and answers step 6's challenge a new way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You cannot free a slave without his consent, since freedom is bad for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money can act against his will, because money can transfer a slave against his will anyway.

steps.title: Then a document should work against his will too
steps.stepSummary: If money works against his will because it can sell him against his will, a שטר should work the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a document should also work this way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי: a slave can also be sold with a document against his will, so others should be able to free him with a document too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reasoning was: whatever can sell the slave against his will can also free him against his will. A document can also sell a slave without his agreement. So by the same reasoning, others should be able to receive his שטר of freedom, which goes against the סיפא.

phrases.notes: He means: a slave can also be sold with a document without his agreement, so the same logic should apply.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reasoning by applying it to a שטר.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason that money frees against his will because it sells against his will.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שטר also sells a slave against his will, so it should also free him through others, but the סיפא says it does not.

steps.title: A bill of sale and a bill of freedom are different documents
steps.stepSummary: The document that sells a slave and the document that frees him are separate things, so you cannot learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This document is separate, and that document is separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: a bill of sale and a שטר of freedom are two different kinds of documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, it is the same money in both cases, so selling and freeing can be compared. A document is different: a bill of sale and a bill of freedom are written differently and do different jobs. So the fact that a bill of sale works against his will says nothing about a bill of freedom.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, for רבי מאיר money can free a slave even without his agreement, because money works the same way in selling and in freeing. A document cannot be received by others, because a bill of sale and a bill of freedom are different documents.

phrases.notes: One is the bill of sale to a new master; the other is the slave's bill of freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שְׁטָרָא לְחוֹד וְהַאי שְׁטָרָא לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and protects אביי's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction between two kinds of documents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A document should be like money: if it sells against his will, it frees against his will.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bill of sale and the bill of freedom are different, so you cannot compare them. Only money can be compared.

steps.title: Isn't Selling Money Different from Freeing Money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on step 14: if the selling document and the freeing document are separate, then the selling money and the freeing money should be separate too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, isn't this money one thing and that money another thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 14. If two documents count as different, why don't two payments count as different too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said money can free the slave against his will because money can sell him against his will. Step 14 said you cannot compare the selling document to the freeing document. So the גמרא asks why we may compare selling money to freeing money.

phrases.notes: He means the money paid to sell the slave to a new master.
And this is the money paid to set him free.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, הַאי כַּסְפָּא לְחוֹד וְהַאי כַּסְפָּא לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the logic of step 14's answer against אביי's comparison of the two kinds of money.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's comparison of selling money to freeing money (step 12)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If separate documents can't be compared, separate payments shouldn't be comparable either.

steps.title: A Coin Is the Same Coin
steps.stepSummary: The coin itself is the same whether it is used to sell or to free, so money can be compared. Documents cannot, because each has its own wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the coin is one and the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that money is money. The same coin could be used to sell the slave or to free him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document is defined by what it says, so a bill of sale and a freedom document really are two different objects. A coin has nothing written on it that ties it to one job. So the comparison between selling money and freeing money still works.

phrases.english: In any case, the coin is one and the same.
phrases.notes: A document's wording changes with its job, but a coin looks the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the physical nature of money from that of a document
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling money and freeing money are as separate as the two documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: The coin is identical in both cases, so the comparison stands. Documents differ in their wording.

steps.title: רבא: Who Receives It Makes the Difference
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different reason why money works through others but a שטר does not: with money the master's receiving it frees the slave, while with a שטר others receive it for the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With money, the master's receiving it is what frees him. With a document, others receiving it is what frees him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers his own explanation of רבי מאיר, in place of אביי's. He points to who actually takes hold of the money or the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, the others give it to the master, and the master taking it frees the slave. Nobody is acquiring anything on the slave's behalf. With a document, the others must receive it for the slave, acting as his agents. That kind of acting for someone against his interest is allowed only in his presence.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא moves the question away from comparing to a sale. He focuses on who is acting in place of the slave.

phrases.english: Money: his master's receiving it brings about [his freedom],
A document: others' receiving it brings about [his freedom].

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כֶּסֶף קַבָּלַת רַבּוֹ גָּרְמָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same question that אביי answered in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different mechanism: who acquires on whose behalf
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Money and a document given by others should work the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: With money, the master's receiving it frees the slave, so nobody acts for him. With a document, others act for him, which needs his presence.

steps.title: The חכמים: Money Only by Himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה and draws the inference that money works by the slave himself but not through others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: With money, by himself. By himself, yes. Through others, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second opinion in the משנה, the חכמים. It reads their words closely, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים flip רבי מאיר's ruling. For them money works when given 'by himself'. The גמרא reads this to mean that money given through others does not work.
steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּכֶסֶף עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי מאיר to the חכמים' half of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, money frees the slave when given by himself, which suggests it does not work through others.

steps.title: Why Can't Others Free Him with Money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why money through others fails for the חכמים. They hold that freedom is a benefit, and you may benefit someone even when he is not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? Even if it is without his consent, the חכמים say freedom is a benefit to him, and we learned that one may benefit a person when he is not there, but act against him only in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 18. If the חכמים say freedom is good for the slave, others should be able to free him even without asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule זכין לאדם שלא בפניו lets anyone act for someone's benefit when he is not there. The חכמים themselves call freedom a benefit. So 'not through others' makes no sense for them.

keyTerms.meaning: one may act for a person's benefit when he is not there

phrases.english: Granted that it is without his consent,
after all, we have heard the Sages say:
for him to go out from under his master's hand to freedom,
One may act for a person's benefit when he is not there,
but one may act against his interest only in his presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference just drawn from the חכמים' words.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that, for the חכמים, money given through others does not free the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חכמים hold freedom is a benefit, and a benefit can be given without the person present, so others should be able to free him.

steps.title: Maybe 'By Himself' Means 'Even by Himself'
steps.stepSummary: A suggested reading: the חכמים mean money works even by himself, not only through others, which teaches that a slave can acquire without his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: 'by himself' means 'even by himself', and it teaches us that a slave can acquire something without his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out. Maybe the חכמים never meant to rule out 'through others'. They were adding that the slave himself can also do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'by himself' means 'even by himself', then others can certainly free him with money, and the challenge in step 19 disappears. The new point would be that a slave can take ownership of something without it automatically going to his master.

keyTerms.meaning: a slave can acquire without his master

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a suggestion, introduced with 'וכי תימא'. The very next step pushes back on it.

phrases.notes: This is the same kind of reading the גמרא tried for רבי מאיר back in step 10.

phrases.english: that a slave can acquire without his master

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מַאי עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ אַף עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 19 by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'By himself' means only by himself and not through others.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'By himself' means even by himself, teaching that a slave can acquire without his master.

steps.title: The Document Clause Doesn't Fit That Reading
steps.stepSummary: If 'by himself' means 'even by himself', then the end of the חכמים' words, 'a document through others', clearly means 'not by himself'. But we hold that a slave's document and his power to receive it come together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end: with a document, through others, and not by himself. But we hold that his document and his power to receive it come at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion in step 20 using the very next clause of the חכמים, the one about the שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים really held that a slave can acquire things himself, they should not limit the שטר to 'through others'. The slave could receive his own document, since his freedom and his power to receive it arrive together. Since the משנה does say 'through others' for the שטר, the 'even by himself' reading looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: his freedom document and his power to receive it come at the same moment

phrases.english: If so, say the end part:
that his document and his hand come at the same time?
phrases.notes: "His hand" means his power to take hold of the document himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: בִּשְׁטָר עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rereading offered in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'even by himself' in the חכמים' money clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read the same way, the document clause excludes 'by himself'. That contradicts the rule that the slave's document and his power to receive it come together, so the reading cannot be right.

steps.title: Maybe 'through others' means 'even through others'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries one more reading: when the חכמים say a שטר works 'through others', they mean 'even through others'. The point would be that freedom is a benefit for the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: what does 'through others' mean? It means 'even through others'. The חכמים are teaching us that it is a benefit for a slave to leave his master and become free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way to answer the challenge of step 21 and save the 'even by himself' reading from step 20. The words 'through others' in the שטר clause would mean 'even through others', not 'only through others'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 showed a problem: if 'through others' means 'not by himself', it goes against the rule that a slave's שטר and his ability to receive it come together. So this reading turns 'through others' into an addition ('even others'). That addition is there to teach that freedom counts as a benefit, so others can receive it for the slave.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.notes: This is the שטר clause of the חכמים: 'a document, through others'.

phrases.english: and this is what it teaches us:
that it is a benefit for a slave
to go out from his master's hand to freedom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מַאי עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים – אַף עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the problem raised in step 21 by reading 'through others' as 'even through others'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Through others' means only through others, and not by the slave himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Through others' means even through others. It teaches that freedom is a benefit, so others can receive it for the slave.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have taught money and document together
steps.stepSummary: If money and a שטר both work through others and by the slave himself, the משנה should have taught them together in one line.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the משנה should have combined them and said: by money and by document, whether through others or by himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reading from step 22. If both methods work exactly the same way, why did the חכמים list them separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under step 22's reading, money works by himself and through others, and so does a שטר. There is no difference between them. Splitting them into two clauses would make sense only if they work differently, so this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it combine them and teach them together

phrases.english: let it combine them and teach them together:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading suggested in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 22 reading, where both money and a שטר work through others and by himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both methods follow the same rule, the משנה would have taught them in one combined clause. The separate clauses show that they are different.

steps.title: The final reading: money both ways, a document only through others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on this reading of the חכמים: money works both through others and by the slave himself, but a שטר works only through others and not by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it like this: by money, whether through others or by himself. By document, through others but not by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: After the other readings were pushed aside, the גמרא gives its final way of reading the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the two clauses really are different, so it makes sense that the משנה taught them separately. Money works either way. A שטר does not work when the slave receives it himself. This still leaves the problem from step 21, which the גמרא handles next by saying this follows one specific תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: By a document (here, a document of freedom)
By himself (the slave receives it himself)

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּכֶסֶף – בֵּין עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים בֵּין עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reading that stands after step 22 was rejected in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Money and a שטר follow one shared rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money works both ways. A שטר works only through others, not by himself.

steps.title: This reading matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a שטר works only through others is the opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as a ברייתא shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, as it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, also with a document, through others but not by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names who holds the rule from step 24 and brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 objected that the usual rule says a slave's שטר and his ability to receive it come together. The גמרא answers that this משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who disagrees with that rule. So the reading stands even though it does not match the usual rule.

phrases.english: And this is the opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Also by a document – through others

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הוּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows which תנא holds the reading from step 24, which answers the objection from step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a שטר works only through others and not by the slave himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: There are three opinions on this question
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר has his own view, there are three different opinions on how a slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are three disputes on this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up. With רבי שמעון בן אלעזר added, there are three opinions on this issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three opinions are those of רבי מאיר, the חכמים, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Each one has a different rule about money versus a שטר, and through others versus by himself.
steps.whatToRemember: For the חכמים' half of the משנה, as the גמרא finally reads it: money works through others and by the slave himself, but a שטר works only through others. That שטר rule is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, one of three opinions (רבי מאיר, the חכמים, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר).

phrases.english: And there are three disputes on this matter.
phrases.notes: The three opinions belong to רבי מאיר, the חכמים, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of steps 24 and 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There are three separate opinions on how a slave goes free.

steps.title: רבה's reason: the slave's שטר is learned from a woman's גט
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר learns from the word 'לה' in both places. Just as a גט must leave the husband's domain, a slave's שטר must leave the master's domain. A slave's hand counts as his master's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר? He learns 'to her' from 'to her' written about a woman. Just as a woman is not divorced until the husband moves the גט into a domain that is not his, so too a slave is not freed until the master moves the שטר into a domain that is not his.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule with a גזירה שוה connecting a slave's freedom to a woman's divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לה' appears both about a maidservant's freedom ('nor was freedom given to her') and about a גט. So the rules of a גט apply to a slave's שטר: the document must leave the giver's domain. Whatever a slave holds still belongs to his master, so giving the שטר into the slave's own hand never takes it out of the master's domain. That is why it works only through others.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns 'to her' from 'to her' (a גזירה שוה)
Into a domain that is not his

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with the usual rule. In his view, a slave's own hand cannot receive his שטר, because it is still his master's hand.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
He learns 'to her' from 'to her' written about a woman:
phrases.notes: The two פסוקים are ויקרא 19:20 (freedom given to her) and דברים 24:1 (he writes for her a גט).

phrases.english: just as a woman is not divorced until he moves the גט
into a domain that is not his,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֶבֶד נָמֵי עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא גֵּט
phrases.english: so too a slave is not freed until he moves the document
into a domain that is not his.
phrases.notes: The slave belongs to the master, so the slave's own hand still counts as the master's domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר brought in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learned from the גט by a גזירה שוה, a slave's שטר must leave the master's domain, so it works only through others.

steps.title: רבה opens a new question
steps.stepSummary: רבה introduces a question he is unsure about. The question itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked a question:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing to present a new question from רבה, and the question itself comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעי shows that רבה is asking something he is unsure about, not attacking an earlier statement. Here it only opens the question, so no content has been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raises a question he is unsure about)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after רבה's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated; the question itself comes on the next amud.
